subject.title: fix(status): use legacy Codex OAuth profiles for OpenAI usage

question: Should `openclaw status --usage` read legacy `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles at runtime for canonical `openai` usage, or should affected users be required to run `openclaw doctor --fix` first?
rationale: Repository policy says legacy `openai-codex` profile ids are migration input repaired by doctor, while this PR deliberately adds a narrow runtime compatibility exception for existing users.

options.title: Confirm the usage-only legacy bridge
options.body: Accept that status/provider-usage may read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

options.title: Keep doctor-only migration
options.body: Close or pause this PR and require users with legacy profile ids to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before usage status reads the credentials.

options.title: Narrow and document the exception
options.body: Require a rebased patch that limits the fallback to the proven status/provider-usage path and documents the doctor/removal boundary.

recommendation.title: Confirm the usage-only legacy bridge
recommendation.body: Accept that status/provider-usage may read retired `openai-codex:*` OAuth/token profiles while still reporting canonical `openai` usage.

likelyOwner.reason: This account authored the provider identity unification and current docs that define canonical `openai` plus doctor-owned legacy repair.
